On Tuesday, Keiko Fujimori will
[become](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/keiko-fujimori-declared-
winner-peru-presidential-race-2026-07-03/) Peru's new president, bringing
[Fujimorismo](https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/keiko-fujimoris-expected-
victory-returns-divisive-dynasty-peru-2026-06-24/), a controversial political
creed, back into the limelight.

After three failed presidential bids since 2011, Fujimori hopes to finally
deliver her vision of a new
"[order](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jun/30/keiko-fujimori-wins-
peru-presidential-election-polls-runoff)" for Peru. But many remain skeptical,
given her family's legacy of corruption. So as Peru prepares for a president
with a deeply divisive surname, here are seven things you need to know.

### 1\. She Is the Daughter of Alberto Fujimori

Alberto Fujimori's decade as president of Peru from 1990 included a bizarre
[self-coup](https://www.newsweek.com/self-coup-rocked-peru-197280), in 1992,
and ended in 2000 in a manner that has become common in Peruvian politics:
amid serious scandal. Triggered by a
[video](https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/politics/2001/03/04/in-peru-
candid-cameras-leave-audience-stunned/7fc056ba-3c4f-4f39-a3b8-16309ccfa2ab/)
of his intelligence chief bribing an opposition congressman, Fujimori's
government [collapsed](https://www.nytimes.com/2000/12/03/world/fujimori-s-
fall-a-nation-s-lion-to-broken-man.html). Eventually, [Fujimori fled to Japan
and resigned by
fax](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2001/sep/16/japan.jonathanwatts).

While supporters credit him for [defeating Shining
Path](https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-16066029), a Maoist rebel
group which fueled decades of violence, Fujimori's legacy is also defined by
[serious human rights abuses](https://www.ictj.org/latest-news/alberto-
fujimori-former-president-peru-who-was-convicted-human-rights-abuses-dies-86)
including death squad killings, civilian disappearances, and forced
sterilization of [thousands of Indigenous
women](https://theconversation.com/fujimoris-death-wont-end-pursuit-of-
justice-for-peruvian-victims-or-stop-the-strongmans-supporters-from-revering-
his-legacy-238944). In 2009, he became the first democratically elected Latin
American leader
[convicted](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2009/apr/07/alberto-fujimori-
peru) [for human rights violations](https://academic.oup.com/ijtj/article-
abstract/3/3/384/2888395?redirectedFrom=PDF), stemming from his role in the
[Barrios Altos and La Cantuta
massacres](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2007/12/22/fujimori-sorry-for-
rights-abuses), in which military death squads killed 25 people, including an
8-year-old boy.
